To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the cell surface marker SUSD2 can be used to identify and purify naive pluripotent stem cell populations.
SUSD2 is expressed in naive hESCs and iPS cells but not in conventional hESCs or somatic cells and is therefore a useful marker for the naive hESC state.
the Sushi Containing domain 2 (SUDS2) protein is a robust cell surface marker of naive human pluripotential stem cells in the embryo and vitro.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the generation of human induced pluripotent stem (iPS) cells from somatic cells and the establishment of human pluripotent cells in a naive state, which is an earlier stage of human pluripotency than conventional human pluripotent cell lines.
the generation, characterisation and application of human pluripotent cells.
the generation and maintenance of naive pluripotent stem cell (nPSCs) lines, and the use of these cell lines in the derivation of induced naive stem cells (iNSCs).
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
SUSD2 is an important marker for naive pluripotency.
SUSD2 is the first cell-surface marker identified for human naive pluripotent stem (hPSC) cells.
SUSD2 is expressed in human epiblasts and is a marker of the human epiblast stem cell state.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
SUSD2 facilitates establishment of human naive pluripotent stem cell.

we have developed a novel, reliable and easy-to-use cell-surface marker for human naive pluripotent stem cell identification and purification, which will facilitate future studies on naive hPSC biology and their applications in regenerative medicine.
we have identified SUSD2 as a robust marker for the naive hPSc state, and that this marker can be used for purification of naive hPSc from conventional hPSc.
The main takeaway from our work is that
SUSD2 is an important cell-surface marker for identifying the naive hPSc phenotype.
the cell-surface protein SUSD2 is an excellent marker of naive hESCs.
the SUSD2 cell-surface marker can be used to reliably discriminate naive human pluripotency.
